description.untrusted_excerpt: A shared workspace for writing documents, sketching on a whiteboard and organising tables in one place, with offline use and live team editing.

claims.untrusted_excerpt: Known gaps: Plugins and third-party add-on blocks are not available yet; the README says they are coming soon.
A shared workspace for writing documents, sketching on a whiteboard and organising tables in one place, with offline use and live team editing.

description.untrusted_excerpt: A Notion-style workspace for notes, documents, task boards and project tables, with desktop and mobile apps and an option to host it on your own server.

claims.untrusted_excerpt: Known gaps: The project states it does not yet claim to match Notion's features or design. The Android app needs Android 10 or above and does not support ARMv7 devices. Self-hosting is covered in a separate guide, not in the README.
A Notion-style workspace for notes, documents, task boards and project tables, with desktop and mobile apps and an option to host it on your own server.

description.untrusted_excerpt: Shared team wiki where people write and edit documents together in real time, with comments, page history, search, permissions and diagrams.

footprint.sentence: Its compose file names these supporting services: postgres, redis. Our rough heuristic, not the project's stated minimum: a small server (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM), for example Hetzner CPX22 in Nuremberg at €19.99 a month excl. VAT (checked 2026-11-24). Check the project's own requirements; this leaves out the time it takes you to run it.

claims.untrusted_excerpt: Known gaps: Enterprise features are not part of the Community Edition and come under a separate enterprise licence.
Shared team wiki where people write and edit documents together in real time, with comments, page history, search, permissions and diagrams.

paid_tool_prices.sentence: Notion Plus starts at $10 a month per seat (billed annually). Billed monthly: $12 a month per seat.

body.order_note: Options are in the order the goal page lists them: by evidence label, then by whether the project is maintained, then by GitHub-star band, then by name. The order is not a judgment of quality, and no vendor can pay for inclusion, position or label.
